steps: Step 1: wallCell (1,0) is not walkable — PathGrid.IsWalkable returns false

Step 3: pawn commanded via SetTarget reaches target OR stops cleanly (LastPathFailed/HasTarget==false) — both outcomes accepted per V8 spec
Step 4: during simulation pawn never occupies cell (1,0) — asserting no clip-through
Step 5: pawn never exits PathGrid bounds — no off-grid stuck

flags_for_qa: FLAG-G1: PawnMovement.UsePathfinding and PawnMovement.Grid are public static fields — the test saves/restores them around the simulation; if another test runs concurrently (parallel test runner) these statics could collide. These tests are designed to run sequentially per the harness.

FLAG-G2: PawnMovement.AdvanceAlongPath drives movement directly (bypasses Unity Update); the pawn is moved at 1.5 * fixedDeltaTime world-units per tick, which is generous for 1-cell grid steps. If PawnStats.CreateDefault().arriveDistance is large the pawn may overshoot the final cell — the test accepts 'arrived OR stopped cleanly' so overshoot is not a failure.

FLAG-G3: No PawnChopper or PawnUtilityAI added to the test pawn — the pawn has no autonomous AI. SetTarget + AdvanceAlongPath is called directly, which is the correct read-only API convention matching prior tests.
FLAG-G4: PathGrid.FromMask indexes as mask[x-MIN, y-MIN] — tested by inspecting PathGrid.cs source. If the MIN offset changes in a future refactor, the mask construction here will need to be updated.
compile_risk: Low — uses only public APIs already used by prior tests. No reflection. No new runtime dependencies. No using directives beyond System.Collections.Generic, UnityEngine, MelonS.GameProto.AI, MelonS.GameProto.Data.
